title: Captured Regions
statement:
Flip every group of `'O'` cells that is completely surrounded by `'X'` cells, modifying the board in place.

Contract
- `board` is a rectangular array of `'X'` and `'O'`; it may have no rows.
- Cells are connected through shared edges only (up, down, left, right). A group of `'O'` cells is safe when any of its cells lies on the outer border of the board; otherwise it is enclosed.
- Change every `'O'` in an enclosed group to `'X'`. Safe groups and all `'X'` cells stay as they are.
- The method returns nothing: the result must be written into `board` itself.

Examples
- Rows `XXXX`, `XOOX`, `XXOX`, `XOXX` become `XXXX`, `XXXX`, `XXXX`, `XOXX`: the bottom `O` is on the border, so only the three inner cells flip.
- Rows `OOO`, `OXO`, `OOO` are unchanged because the ring of `O` cells touches the border.
- Rows `XXXXX`, `XOXOX`, `XXOXX` become `XXXXX`, `XXXXX`, `XXOXX`.
hints: An O group survives exactly when it can reach the border, so ask which cells are safe rather than which are enclosed.
Start from every O on the border and spread through connected O cells, marking them with a temporary symbol. Anything still O afterwards is enclosed.
Finish with one pass that turns the marked cells back into O and the remaining O cells into X. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space for the traversal stack, where n is the number of cells.
inputSyntax: Input: the board rows separated by spaces, using X and O, for example: XXXX XOOX XXOX XOXX
